why: accuracy: lungs don’t let a turtle breathe underwater; it holds its breath. Also defines “predators”
old: A turtle's shell (external) protects it from predators. The turtle's lungs (internal) let it breathe air, even underwater for short trips.
new: A turtle's shell (external) protects it from predators (animals that hunt it). The turtle's lungs (internal) let it breathe air, then hold that air on short dives underwater.

why: accuracy: mangrove roots hold the tree up and take in air (not just “breathe”); also plain-language rewrite of the box
old: Plant structures aren't random — they're adaptations that help plants survive in their specific environment. A cactus in a desert has thick, waxy skin to hold water and sharp spines instead of leaves to keep animals from eating it. A mangrove tree along Florida's coast has tangled roots that rise above the water, helping it breathe in salty, muddy soil. A Venus flytrap in poor soil traps insects to get the nutrients the soil can't provide.
new: Plant structures aren't random. They're adaptations (body parts that help a living thing survive where it lives). A desert cactus has thick, waxy skin to hold water and sharp spines to keep animals from eating it. A mangrove tree on Florida's coast has tangled roots that arch above the water and mud. They hold the tree up and take in air. A Venus flytrap grows in poor soil, so it traps insects to get the nutrients (the healthy stuff a living thing needs) the soil doesn't have.

why: “misconception” → plain words; shorter; dashes removed
old: Common misconception: Some people think a structure exists "in order to" help an animal — like the animal asked for it. That's not quite right. Structures developed slowly, over many generations, because the animals with the most useful structures were the ones most likely to survive and have babies. The structure didn't plan ahead — it just turned out to work.
new: A mix-up to watch for: Animals don't choose their body parts. Over many, many generations, animals with the most useful parts were the most likely to survive and have babies. The babies got those parts too.
